answer: Here is one mechanism that works: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because tundra only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, onyx is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any summit approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
